human_tolerance.notes: Common in wooded suburbs and even in city parks, drumming on buildings, gutters and transformer boxes as well as on dead wood.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Resident all year on its range, holding a territory and calling and drumming in every season; males call and drum more than females and both sexes call.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: In early May both sexes begin breeding activities with drumming patterns such as slow taps followed by short rapid drumming; both sexes dig the nesting cavity and mark the area around it with drilling holes.

vocalizations.description: One of a varied repertoire of loud rattling calls, given by both sexes through the year and used to keep a pair together; the drumming itself - slow taps followed by short rapid drumming - carries much of the same message.
A harsh alarm call, given either while hiding from a predator or while harassing it.

range.note: Resident across the eastern United States; it is expanding northwards into Canada, which is not listed as native here.

traits.limb_count.note: Biped: two legs; the wings are not counted as limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Clings to and climbs tree trunks and flies between trees.

traits.nest_type.note: Nests in decayed cavities of dead trees, old stumps, or in live trees with softer wood such as elms, maples or willows; both sexes dig the cavity.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 69.5 g converted to kilograms; Wikipedia gives 2.0-3.2 oz, which is 56.7-90.6 g.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia gives 22.85-26.7 cm; the midpoint is used.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the 38-46 cm wingspan given on Wikipedia.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No allow-listed open source states wild longevity for this species. Authored estimate only: 6 years, taken as the mid-range figure for a small woodpecker and not a sourced datum. Treat it as an order-of-magnitude value.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 30 mapped to 'invertebrate', Diet-Vend 10 and Diet-Vect 10 summed to 'vertebrate' 0.1, Diet-Fruit 20 to 'fruit', Diet-Seed 20 to 'seed' and Diet-Nect 10 to 'nectar'; the dataset classes this species as an omnivore. Wikipedia notes it also takes the eggs of box-nesting wood ducks in parts of its range.

traits.social.note: A territorial pair holds and defends a cavity nest site, and both parents share incubation and chick-rearing duties.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0; Wikipedia describes a bird that calls and drums through the day in every season.

traits.defense.note: Wikipedia states that, approached by a predator, it either hides from it or harasses it with alarm calls; Hide is used for the more usual response.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: bold around buildings and feeders, drumming on human structures rather than avoiding them, but it still retreats into the canopy when closely approached.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value gives midhigh 20 / canopy 60 / aerial 20 and no ground component; the midhigh and canopy strata are summed into the arboreal share, keeping aerial separate.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts and nests in cavities in dead and drying wood.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the nesting weights are judgement, since no open source gives their relative use.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia describes it tapping on hollow trees and on aluminium roofs, metal guttering and transformer boxes in urban environments.

seasonal.strategy.note: Resident all year on its range, with no migration.

seasonal.phases.note: Year-round calling and drumming, the early-May start of breeding activities and the shared cavity digging are from Wikipedia; the narrow May-June breeding window is authored judgement, since no open source gives egg dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Wikipedia says fledglings beg from their parents for a while after leaving the nest but gives no interval; the 60-day juvenile window and the 0.85 scale are authored judgement.

vocalizations.contact_call.note: Wikipedia describes this species as noisy with many varied calls, and gives the drumming pattern that precedes breeding; the specific call wording and the cooldown are authored. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

vocalizations.alarm_call.note: Wikipedia states it hides from a predator or harasses it with alarm calls; the wording and the cooldown are authored.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description: light grey face and underparts, black-and-white barring on back, wings and tail, a vivid orange-red crown and nape in the male, and a long chisel bill. The proportions and the crown and barred-back boxes are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. Woodpeckers do not sing and do not forage on the ground, so this is a compromise: the tree is a perching-and-fleeing tree, and the slot the program uses for a song is given to the pair's contact call and drumming. It gleans insects from bark and takes nest cavities between May and June.
